summary.headline: Timken India Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~15% YoY to INR929 crore, with PBT of INR150 crore and PBT margin of 16.2%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR929 crore, up almost 15% YoY, after a seasonally strong Q4 FY26 (highest standalone revenue of INR3,147 crore for FY26). PBT rose to INR150 crore from INR130 crore, with PBT margin at 16.2% versus 16.1% a year earlier, and EBITDA margin at 19.6%. Gross margin was 39.9%, up 100 bps YoY and roughly flat QoQ, which management attributed to heavy-truck and off-highway price increases offsetting unfavourable Q1 mix. The Bharuch plant is ramping up quickly, with revenue of about INR50 crore in the quarter and near breakeven.

segments.name: Rail
segments.commentary: INR200 crore, about 22% of Q1 revenue. Management described government railway buying as slow and sluggish, and said the year started with about 3% growth in rail.

segments.name: Mobile / others
segments.commentary: INR184 crore. Management said mobile (tractors, heavy trucks) is about 20% of the business and is where price increases are sticking.

segments.name: Process
segments.commentary: INR186 crore, up about 28-30% YoY, driven by metals customers and wind (gearbox exports and domestic wind farms).

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About INR200 crore, including about 1% export incentive. Intercompany push to America rose about 21%; Europe is down, China and ASEAN are down, and the US is up.

segments.name: Bharuch plant (within segments)
segments.commentary: About INR50 crore revenue in Q1, close to breakeven. Spherical roller bearing (SRB) line utilisation was about 40-45% in Q1, targeted at about 70% by August-September; CRB line utilisation is lower, with ramp toward Q2-end and Q3.

guidance_outlook: Bharuch SRB line expected to reach about 70% utilisation in August-September 2026; CRB line ramp toward end of Q2 and Q3.
Rail expansion at Jamshedpur expected to start commercial production by calendar year-end 2026; management said it will ramp up immediately after that.
FY27 capex expected at about 8-10% of sales, with project work described as on track; timing may spill some capex into FY28.
Further cost escalation seen as limited beyond the steel, carbide, coal and grinding increases already in the system; base oil described as the only volatile input.
Management said it will continue to pass on cost increases to heavy-truck and off-highway customers as contracts renew; rail and PSU/ARC contracts are fixed and will reprice only at renewal.
capex_capacity: Bharuch plant ramping up; three manufacturing lines; utilisation cannot be given at plant level but SRB demand is higher than CRB at this stage.
Rail investment at Jamshedpur on track; plain bearings investment at Bharuch on track.
Manufactured vs traded mix roughly 75/25, similar to prior quarters.
Gas conversion from LPG to natural gas completed across supply chain and plants.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth driven by resilient core-segment demand and both export and domestic execution.
Steel producers raised prices by about INR1,500-1,600 per tonne in January and about INR3,500 per tonne by April, around INR5,000 per tonne in total; most customers have started paying the increase.
Price pass-through is working in heavy truck and tractor/off-highway; rail, PSU and cement customers are on fixed annual rate contracts.
Process growth partly from metals projects (mills built in India for export) and wind.
Management said the US market is up, Europe and China are down, and ASEAN and Australia are flat to down.
No direct tariff figure given; management said the US landed tariff has moved over time and it would confirm the current rate.
Management said the parent's 80/20 portfolio review is aimed at performance improvement; no change in Indian strategy was announced.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split for Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Rail INR200 crore (22%), mobile/others INR184 crore, distribution INR153.9 crore, process INR186 crore, exports about INR200 crore including 1% export incentive.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of parent's 80/20 strategy and belts divestment on India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 80/20 is a Pareto-based performance tool that is being applied globally; it is not yet a change in strategy for India. The India focus stays on off-highway, rail and tractor/heavy-truck, with no two-wheeler, passenger car or washing-machine ball bearings.

qa_highlights.question: Bharuch ramp-up and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Bharuch revenue was about INR50 crore, close to breakeven. SRB utilisation was about 40-45% in Q1, expected to reach about 70% by August-September; CRB is lower with ramp toward Q2-end and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of process and export growth and US outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Process grew about 30% YoY, from metals and wind. Exports to the US are growing, Europe is down, and the intercompany push to America is about 21%.

qa_highlights.question: Rail outlook and Jamshedpur ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Government railway procurement is slow due to funds diverted to infrastructure and defence; management expects this to be timing-related. Jamshedpur rail capacity is due to start commercial production by calendar year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cost inflation has been passed through to price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to give an exact percentage; heavy truck and tractor customers have largely passed through cost escalation, while rail and PSU contracts will reprice at renewal.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 capex plan and allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant-wise split not given; capex directionally in line with the 8-10% of sales range, with some timing spillover into the next fiscal.

risks_watch: Steel and other input cost inflation: about INR5,000 per tonne of steel price increases; pass-through is incomplete for rail and PSU contracts that are fixed until renewal.
Slow government railway procurement due to fund diversion to infrastructure and defence; it could delay the Jamshedpur ramp-up benefit.
Bharuch ramp-up needs to reach about 70% SRB utilisation by August-September and CRB later; any slippage would weigh on margins.
Parent's 80/20 review and divestments (belts, automotive OE): the Indian implications are unclear, and management said it will review which assets can be used for growth in India.
Export exposure to geopolitics; Europe, China and ASEAN are down; US tariff status was not confirmed on the call.
Base oil price volatility affecting grease costs; the Brent outlook and the Middle East conflict affect energy and gas costs.
NCLT approval of the Timken GGB Technology merger is pending.
key_quotes: We have delivered high double-digit revenue growth this quarter Y-o-Y, driven by resilient demand, especially in the core segments, and our execution both for export and domestic.
So, the revenues are growing with every passing week, and I will ask Sujit to add more colour to the whole thing so that you get a little bit more specific answer.
So railway is a little bit sluggish as we speak, but it is an issue of time, so it will come back.
It is tough to tell you exactly percentage. Different customers, different behaviour.
summary.management_tone: Management sounded confident on Q1 execution, Bharuch ramp-up pace and cost pass-through in heavy-truck and tractor markets. It was cautious and deferred on exact price-recovery percentages, rail timing, US tariff rate and future cost escalation tied to the Middle East conflict and Brent.
